name: Ali Khamenei
summary: Khamenei led Iran as Supreme Leader for 37 years under the doctrine of clerical guardianship, defending an Islamic republic he called religious democracy against Western liberal models. He combined support for privatization and self-reliance with state control of culture and dissent, conservative views on gender and family, and fierce opposition to the United States and Israel. He backed civilian nuclear work while reportedly forbidding nuclear weapons by fatwa.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 2018 Blueprint guidelines he issued set 'complete coverage of care and services and the fair distribution of health resources' as a national strategy, without saying the state must fund all care.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pushed privatization (2007, Article 44) and criticized unnecessary state interference, while also favouring a state-guided resistance economy and self-reliance.

public-ownership.rationale: Mixed: the Article 44 policies he issued moved most state enterprises to private and cooperative hands, and he said government cannot manage large production companies, but oil, gas and 'public property rights over natural resources' stay public in his own texts (2018 Blueprint).

property-fundamental.rationale: Suggested courts protect ownership rights to encourage private investment (2007).

legalize-drugs.rationale: His rulings state that using narcotics in any way is forbidden because of the harm to health and the social cost, that dealing in them is forbidden in any form, and that relatives should report traffickers to the authorities (medical use excepted).

strong-leader.rationale: Expanded the Leader's control over state institutions and said power must be used rather than wasted.

state-harmful.rationale: His rulings say every society needs a guardian, ruler and leader to defend it, keep its order and establish justice, so a society without a state is not acceptable.

empower-police-military.rationale: Built up the IRGC as an instrument of domestic control and regional influence.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: He criticised the promotion of promiscuity and prostitution in Western societies as decadence and a 'sex trade' that destroys families (2023).

traditional-family.rationale: Backed pronatalist policy, gender segregation and criticized Western treatment of women and family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Described homosexuality as a moral deprivation found in the West.

abortion-legal.rationale: His rulings state that abortion is forbidden, not permitted for economic hardship or for a deformed fetus, and allowed only where the mother's life is endangered (before ensoulment, with blood money in some cases).

more-religion-public.rationale: Led a state built on Islamic principles in public life and praised religious democracy as still attractive when liberal democracy had lost appeal (2006).

gender-social-construct.rationale: Described gender equality as a plot to corrupt women's role in society, implying distinct natural roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Warned against Western cultural influence and praised Persian as the language of revolutionary Islam.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Mixed: he called the UN Security Council illogical, unjust and undemocratic (2012) and asked for a participatory, democratic global management, but did not call for giving the UN more power as such.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: At the 2012 Non-Aligned Summit he criticised states that protect Western interests in the name of 'human rights' and interfere militarily in other countries in the name of 'democracy'; he also opposed NATO's 2011 Libya intervention.

limit-growth.rationale: He urged continuous economic growth as the key to improving the country, while his environment policies require sustainability standards and compensation for polluters; he did not call for limiting growth.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Supported civilian nuclear technology and endorsed the 2015 nuclear deal.

revolution-justified.rationale: He celebrated the 1979 Revolution as the uprooting of a tyrannical monarchy and called the Revolution's slogans enduring (2019, 2024).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2025 he objected to lifting the ban on imports that have a domestic equivalent ('Why should it be lifted? Promote what is produced domestically'), and his policies call for increasing domestic manufacture of imported goods.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His policies direct the state to prioritise strategic products and services and to guide public liquidity into production; in 2025 he urged the Central Bank and ministries to steer people's money toward productive investment.

one-party-rule.rationale: In 2007 he presented religious democracy as a course that saves humanity from systems founded on individual or party dictatorship or the influence of the wealthy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He called the Pahlavi and Qajar monarchy a tyranny, said the Revolution uprooted a 'treacherous, corrupt and immoral' monarchy, and described the Revolution as turning that system into a democratic one.

democracy-best.rationale: Called elections a pivot of religious democracy but argued liberal democracy had lost its appeal and the Guardian Council he oversaw disqualified many candidates; position is mixed.

right-to-secede.rationale: He described separatism as an enemy plot (2022-2023) and praised the youth of Hamedan and Kermanshah who fought separatists in the west of the country in the Revolution's first days.

political-violence-never.rationale: He endorsed the revolution against the Shah and praised armed resistance by Palestinian and Lebanese groups against Israel as legitimate, at the same time condemning terrorism against civilians (e.g. 2001, 2004).

separate-church-state.rationale: Rejected the Western liberal model in favour of religious democracy and ran a system fusing clerical and state authority.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Presided over a system where laws must conform to Islamic criteria and the Guardian Council can veto bills on that ground (Arts. 4, 91, 96); defended it as religious democracy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He described Iran as a nation of many ethnic groups and Islamic denominations (Persian, Baluch, Kurdish and others) whose unity he defended, and said Islamic civilization honours people for their humanity, not their ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: In 2025 he described the idea that conflict and contradiction drive social, political and economic history as a flawed Marxist notion that misled people for years, and said Islam teaches the opposite.

civilizational-union.rationale: He called for Islamic unity as a belief, not a tactic, and for the Islamic world to cooperate against its enemies; he did not propose a single political state.

limit-population.rationale: Called for rising population and opposed measures to reduce it (see pronatalist policy reported in the opened article).

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mixed: in 2022 he said capitalism views workers as tools to be exploited for the owner's wealth and condemned owners who strip factories or withhold wages, but he also said workers and entrepreneurs are 'two wings' who should each get a fair share, and that seeking wealth is not a crime.

taxation-theft.rationale: His rulings say it is not permissible to evade taxes, duties and other legal payments to the state, even to a state that is not Islamic, and that false price declarations to cut stamp duty are wrong.

harm-principle.rationale: In 2019 he said social freedom is the right of every person to decide, act and think, but that it must not be defined in opposition to divine ethics, laws, values and public rights.

universal-morality.rationale: The 2018 Blueprint he issued says moral merits are rooted in reality, their principles constant, absolute and comprehensive, and discoverable through reason and nature, with details from the Quran and Sunnah.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Called Israel a 'brutal Zionist regime', a 'cancerous tumor' and said it would not exist in 25 years.

school-vouchers.rationale: In 2025 he said the education system is a governmental institution and it is the Islamic government's duty to teach youth through high school, and he rejected proposals to hand parts of it to other entities as fragmenting and senseless.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In 2023 he called a budget deficit 'a great economic disaster' and criticised budget laws that approve fixed spending against uncertain revenue; he also objected to money printing out of proportion to production (2021).

national-self-determination.rationale: He said the people of Palestine should elect their own government and run their own country, and praised nations asserting independence from domineering powers.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The 2018 Blueprint he issued says Islam insists on reason and human knowledge but treats revelation as a means to sound reasoning and seeks no contradiction between reason and hadith, science and religion; it does not make reason alone the guide.

class-collaboration.rationale: In 2022 he called workers and entrepreneurs 'the two wings of a flight', and in 2025 he rejected the Marxist view of the workplace as a site of conflict between worker and owner, proposing profit-sharing that benefits both.

dominated-front.rationale: Cast the US as the leading force of imperialism, opposed Western dominance, and rejected talks with Washington (Feb 2025).

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Believed in gender segregation and called equality a plot to corrupt women's role, while stating women may take part in political and social life.

ban-interest.rationale: His published rulings state that ribā (interest on loans) is forbidden, and the 2018 Blueprint guidelines he issued call for 'getting rid of loan usury' in the banking system; he accepts Iranian bank contracts only where they take a recognised Islamic form.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Called for using oil and gas reserves to make Iran an energy superpower (2007), though he also criticized oil dependence.

national-mission.rationale: His foreign policy centred on exporting the Islamic revolution; he framed the Arab Spring as an Islamic awakening.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He ruled that the leader must also secure the means of cultural, political and social development and prosperity for society and stop the strong from victimising the weak; his policies also have the state direct economic, family and cultural policy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: He described Israel as created by Western colonial governments, which imported thousands of settlers and armed groups to occupy Palestine and expel its people (2011, 2024).

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: In 2020 he said the education system must pursue the same goal as the whole system, an Islamic society based on justice, so state schooling is meant to carry Islamic teaching.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mixed: in 2024 he said that in the system 'the people are the owners' who choose and vote, and that the people's participation is the foundation of an 'Islamic Republic', yet his rulings place final authority in the jurist leader under divine law and the Guardian Council vets candidates.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: His rulings allow the qualified jurist leader to declare jihad against unbelievers when expediency requires, and require the state to enforce Islamic penal codes, so he did not hold that initiating force is always wrong.

separated-powers.rationale: He called for the judiciary to act independently of executive officials (2022) and listed judicial independence in the 2018 Blueprint, while the Leader himself stands above the three branches.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He told officials to care for the weaker classes and poor regions (2017) and criticised weak progress on social justice and relieving the deprived (2022); this stops short of a rule giving the poor first priority in law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He described Iran's young, growing population as an 'opportunity and advantage' for national power and a 'valuable asset' (2014, 2019), the opposite of treating population growth as the main cause of poverty.

party-controls-media.rationale: Controlled media through his office's influence and blocked a 2000 press-law reform; critics report persecution for insulting the leader.

party-commands-army.rationale: The 2016 General Policies on Elections he issued prohibit the armed forces from entering political and partisan arenas or backing candidates; he commanded the armed forces himself as Leader, not through a party.

head-commands-forces.rationale: As Leader he was commander-in-chief of the armed forces and appointed their commanders by edict; ministers are chosen by the president with the Majlis, not by him.

clerical-rule.rationale: As Supreme Leader he held the highest political authority as the qualified jurist under velayat-e faqih (constitution Arts. 5, 109, 113).

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Issued a 1996 fatwa against promoting music in schools and urged poetry to serve the revolution.

death-penalty.rationale: In 2018 he commanded the head of the judiciary to enforce God's hudud penalties on the convicted perpetrators of a school crime, and his rulings say Islamic penal codes must be enforced even in the Imam's occultation.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Reportedly issued a fatwa forbidding production, stockpiling and use of nuclear weapons, cited by Iran at the IAEA in 2005; its status is questioned by some experts.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He defended choosing the Leader, the head of state, indirectly through the elected Assembly of Experts rather than by direct vote (2024).

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He praised those who fought separatists in the west of the country in the first days of the Revolution, and he called separatist groups enemy-backed.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His rulings say the leader's edicts must be issued in accordance with Islamic jurisprudence, that abrogating Islamic rules is impossible, and that a leader who reached office by the known legal process must be obeyed; he did not place the ruler above Islamic law.

refugee-return.rationale: He said Palestine must be returned to its Palestinian owners, who should decide the status of the Zionists (2024), and is reported (2009) as proposing that Palestinian refugees return and a government be chosen without immigrant Jews.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: His rulings state that Islamic penal codes must be enforced, and he called Rushdie an apostate and endorsed the sentence against him; the same rulings say neglect of prayer or fasting alone does not make someone an apostate.

women-must-cover.rationale: Defended compulsory hijab as honouring women and answered Western objections to it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: In 2023 he called a mandatory 25 percent female quota in offices 'wrong' and said the criterion should be merit, not a set percentage.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He called the Pahlavi and Qajar dynasties tyrannical and, in a 2020 Hajj message, set 'discrimination and aristocratic privileges' against the ideal Islamic community.

delink-world-market.rationale: In 2019 he said independence should not be defined as confining a country's politics and economy within its borders, and his Resistance Economy policies call for an outward-looking economy with expanded exports and regional trade ties.

elective-rulers.rationale: In 2024 he said that after the Revolution the people choose lawmakers and the president, and choose the Leader through the Assembly of Experts, contrasting this with the earlier monarchy.

parliament-supreme.rationale: In 2020 he endorsed Khomeini's view that the Majlis is the highest echelon of national affairs and defines the country's path through law; in his view the Leader and Guardian Council still oversee its laws.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He argued the clergy should not stay neutral or avoid politics and that voting is necessary and obligatory (2024, 2025); he criticised the view that political activity is contrary to religion's sanctity.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Promoted self-reliance and a resistance economy, urged domestic production and warned against making the economy dependent on sanctions relief.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said religious democracy derived from Islamic doctrine is distinct from, and more attractive than, Western liberal democracy.

filial-duty.rationale: His 2014 population policy and 2016 family policy call for a culture of respecting the aged, keeping them within families, and providing them physical, psychological and emotional care.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: His Resistance Economy policies call for managing consumption and reforming consumption norms, the 2016 family policies call for fighting 'aristocratic behavior, extravagance', and his rulings call consumption beyond one's requirements wastefulness.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Backed the Axis of Resistance and hosted Hamas leaders, praising their struggle (Feb 2025).

corporate-influence.rationale: He described Western democracy as 'money-based', driven by capital and by Zionist capitalists' sway over politicians, in messages between 2006 and 2022; this concerns Western systems rather than Iran.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Reversed his earlier acceptance of birth control and backed population-growth policy; Iran adopted childbirth incentives. Only a caption in the opened article attributes the 150 million target to him.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: His rulings say it is not permissible to break the rules of the Islamic Republic (for example by smuggling) and that one should observe the law of the land where ignoring it would cause chaos or violate others' rights, though a state law contrary to Islamic injunctions is not to be obeyed.

non-intervention.rationale: Mixed: he condemned outside intervention in other states' affairs, but Iran under him sent forces and arms to Syria, Iraq and elsewhere, which he defended as help to governments that asked for it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: In 2024 he criticised people who take pride in using foreign words instead of the Persian equivalent as a sign of cultural captivity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He repeatedly said liberalism and communism have lost their appeal and exposed their flaws, called capitalism discriminatory and money-driven, and presented Islam and 'religious democracy' as the new course for humanity (2004-2022).

holocaust-denial.rationale: Referred to 'the myth of the massacre of Jews' (2006) and said in 2014 that the Holocaust's reality was uncertain; Iran's foreign minister later said remarks were mistranslated. Contested.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: from his repeated description of legalising homosexuality as a scandal and moral corruption that is forbidden in all divine religions; he did not specify a criminal penalty in the texts reviewed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Sidelined leftist factions, moderate clerics and dissidents; protests in 2009, 2017-19, 2022-23 were repressed under his rule; urged judges to crack down on dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He described Salman Rushdie as a renegade 'sentenced to capital punishment' and praised Khomeini for not yielding on that ruling (2005, 2011), while his rulings treat Jews, Christians and Zoroastrians as People of the Book with whom social contact is permitted.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: His rulings say defending Islam and Muslims is obligatory and needs no parental permission, and that Muslims must obey the leader's call to defend against aggressive infidels; he called the Sacred Defense a religious duty and the Palestinian cause a religious obligation of the whole Muslim world (2021).

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Defended the constitutional order in which sovereignty belongs to God (Art. 56) and contrasted religious democracy with liberal democracy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: In 2020 he called defensive power vital to every country and nation, one of the three pillars of national power, and warned of what happens to nations deprived of it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He listed non-alignment with any power bloc among the Non-Aligned Movement's core values (2012) and stressed Khomeini's 'Neither East nor West' (2022); Iran joined no military bloc under him.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that the educational system's goal is to build an Islamic society, with Quranic and religious education throughout schooling.

abolish-ip.rationale: His rulings treat authors', translators' and publishers' rights as real: as a matter of caution, permission should be sought before reprinting or copying works, and authors may claim payment and shares of later editions.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He said US military bases in the region are paid for by the poor host countries and that the Americans must leave Iraq and Syria.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He consistently honoured those killed for the Revolution, the Sacred Defense and the Resistance as martyrs with the highest rank before God, in condolence messages and speeches.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He described the Revolution as speaking of 'benefiting from both religion and the material world' and listed spirituality and ethics among his core recommendations; he framed religious democracy as saving people from materialism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: His rulings hold that the jurist leader may declare jihad against unbelievers when he judges expediency requires it ('the strongest opinion'), which goes beyond purely defensive war, although his public line was that Iran does not seek to start wars.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: He repeatedly said the US and other enemies backed separatist groups and plotted separatism and ethnic discord to weaken Iran (2022, 2023, 2013).

pollution-taxes.rationale: His 2015 General Policies on the Environment call for 'green taxes' among the means of encouraging environment-friendly investment and for punishing polluters and forcing them to compensate.

future-generations.rationale: The 2018 Blueprint guidelines call for exploiting natural resources with 'intergenerational' considerations, and the 2015 environment policies call for sustainability standards and management of vital resources.

capital-controls.rationale: In 2025 he called the repatriation of foreign-exchange earnings by exporters, including large state companies, very important and urged channelling savings from gold and foreign currency purchases into production; he did not describe broader controls on capital flows.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The 2015 environment policies call for an environmental auditing system that counts environmental values and costs (destruction, pollution, revival) in national accounting.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The 2018 Blueprint he issued describes an inborn human nature from the divine breath, with innate goodness and rights, to which Islam is said to correspond.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: from his statements that nuclear weapons do not ensure security, that nuclear states' doctrines should be rejected and condemned, and that all should be disposed of; he did not address unilateral disarmament directly.

premarital-sex.rationale: He said sexual freedom and promiscuity in the West destroy the family, and his family policies call for Islamic relations between men and women and honour within marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Ordered the National Information Network and set up the Supreme Council of Cyberspace; opposed unbridled internet access. Interpretation of shutdowns is partly the cited author's.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said women may take part in political, cultural and social life and called denying them education or choice in marriage oppression; female suffrage continued under him.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: He argued that Islam honours women and equals them with men in human and spiritual value, and that it is Western culture and capitalism that oppress and exploit women (2021, 2023).

international-criminal-courts.rationale: In 2021 he said Netanyahu and the Israeli agents responsible for the Gaza killings should be prosecuted and punished by independent international courts; in 2007 he predicted US officials would be tried over Iraq.

indirect-election.rationale: He defended selecting the Leader through the Assembly of Experts, itself elected by the people, as 'a demonstration of Islamic democracy' (2024).

no-business-privileges.rationale: In 2019 he said that giving special privileges to some, discriminating in the distribution of public resources and tolerating economic fraudsters are strictly forbidden, and in 2024 he told the Central Bank not to let state-owned or well-connected companies take scarce bank credit unfairly.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: His 2018 Blueprint and 2019 statement set a goal of a knowledge-based, self-sufficient economy and science leadership grounded in Islamic spirituality and 'Islamic-Iranian' values, and in 2004 he said Iran had intertwined technology and scientific knowledge with moral and spiritual values.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 2018 Blueprint guidelines he issued call for maintaining public property rights over natural resources and national wealth, and he praised the oil nationalisation movement of 1950-51 as a turning point (2025).

multipolar-world.rationale: In 2012 he said global developments promise a multi-faceted order in which traditional power blocs are replaced by a group of countries and civilizations, and that world management should not be the dictatorial will of a few Western states.

notes:
Khamenei died on 28 February 2026 (Wikipedia). No answer is marked Inferred: each rests on stated views or record as reported in the opened sources. Many themes (taxation, welfare, ecology, technology, most institutional design questions) are null because no reliable position was found in opened sources. Holocaust remarks are contested (mistranslation claim). Opened sources are mostly secondary reports of his speeches; khamenei.ir could not be fetched.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Historical figure (died 28 February 2026): all answers rest on his own texts or on his record in office, none are inferred. Answers use his mature positions as Supreme Leader; his 1980s positions as president and in the Majlis were not weighted separately. Where his words and his record diverge (open protest versus repression of 'sedition', non-alignment versus Russia and China ties, non-intervention versus Iran's regional role) the answer is mixed at low confidence. Sources are the official English site KHAMENEI.IR (speeches, messages, policy decrees), his published rulings (Practical Laws of Islam, Medical Issues) and Wikipedia for dates and summaries.
